name: 手打ちそば 花もも (Teuchi Soba Hanamomo)

claims.text: This is not a gluten-free or celiac-safe restaurant. The house soba is nihachi (二八) soba, explicitly an 80% buckwheat / 20% wheat-flour blend, so the noodles themselves contain wheat.

Wheat flour is worked and stone-ground buckwheat is handled throughout the kitchen every morning, so flour in the air and on surfaces makes cross-contamination unavoidable for anyone strictly avoiding gluten.

Soba here is served with a soy-sauce-based dipping tsuyu (and broth-based dishes like duck nanban use the same style of seasoning). Japanese soy sauce is typically brewed with wheat, adding another source of gluten beyond the noodles.

There are no documented vegan or vegetarian-specific options. Soba tsuyu and broths are traditionally built on katsuobushi (bonito) dashi, and popular dishes feature duck, so even a plain bowl of soba is very unlikely to be vegan. No source describes any plant-based preparation or separate vegan handling.

No allergy-handling protocol, gluten-free accommodation, or dietary statement is documented in any available source. Diners with celiac disease or serious allergies should contact the shop directly to confirm before visiting.

name: 富小路 天ぷらまつ井 (Tominokoji Tempura Matsui)

claims.text: This is a tempura specialist: items are coated in wheat-flour batter and deep-fried, so the food is not celiac-safe. A shared frying oil handling many wheat-battered items makes gluten cross-contamination effectively unavoidable.
No dedicated gluten-free fryer or separate-oil arrangement is documented in any source.

Tempura is served with tentsuyu (a dashi-and-soy dipping sauce) and/or salt; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat, and tentsuyu and any dashi base typically include wheat-containing soy and/or other wheat-derived seasonings. Treat the sauces as gluten-containing unless the kitchen confirms otherwise.

Vegetable tempura exists, but the batter, the shared frying oil (used for fish, prawn and other animal items), and dashi/tentsuyu (made with bonito and other fish stock) mean vegetable items are not vegan and carry heavy animal cross-contact. No vegan-specific preparation is documented.

No documented allergy or gluten-free accommodation was found in available sources. The chef does discuss the day's ingredients with guests at the counter, so allergen questions can be raised directly - but confirm any needs in advance.
Small ten-seat counter where the chef fries to order in front of you and talks guests through the day's ingredients, making it easy to ask about preparation directly.
Tempura is fried low and light, and is noted as eating less heavy than typical tempura - though this does not change its gluten or animal-product content.

Tonga is not celiac-safe. The core menu is panko-breaded, deep-fried tonkatsu and other fried yoshoku (shrimp fry, cream croquettes, chicken katsu) cooked in shared fryer oil, with wheat flour in the breading and batter. No gluten-free accommodation is documented and no dedicated fryer is mentioned.
Signature dishes are finished with a house-made demi-glace-style sauce, which is typically thickened with wheat flour, an added gluten source on top of the breading.

Yoshoku and tonkatsu seasonings here rely on soy- and dashi-based flavorings, and most Japanese soy sauce contains wheat. Assume gluten is present in the sauces and seasonings unless staff confirm otherwise.

There is no documented vegan or vegetarian option. The menu centers on pork, lamb, beef, chicken, and seafood, sides such as miso soup and the demi-glace-style sauce are likely animal- and dashi-based, and everything fried shares oil with meat and seafood. Treat as unsuitable for strict vegan diets.
グルテンフリー対応や専用調理に関する記載は確認できませんでした。クラシックな喫茶店であり、ムースケーキなど提供される洋菓子・軽食は小麦の使用が前提です。セリアック（小麦アレルギー）の方には安全とは言えません。
看板のウインナー珈琲は珈琲＋ホイップ生クリームで、乳製品を含みます。植物性ミルク等の代替や、ヴィーガン対応の記載は確認できませんでした。対応可否は来店前に直接確認してください。
アレルギー対応や除去食、コンタミ管理に関する具体的な情報は見つかりませんでした。詳細はスタッフに直接ご確認ください。

name: 洋食の店　みしな (Yoshoku no Mise Mishina)

claims.text: This is a classic yoshoku fry restaurant built on wheat: crab cream croquettes, shrimp fry and fried sets use wheat-flour breading and batter, the signature beef stew is built on a roux-based two-week demi-glace, and the cream filling is flour-thickened. It is not celiac-safe and no gluten-free accommodation is documented.

The kitchen is a single small counter (about ten seats) where breaded fried items and flour-based sauces are the core of the menu, so cross-contamination of any non-fried dish with wheat is highly likely. There is no evidence of a separate fryer or allergen-segregated prep.

Meals are finished with ochazuke and pickles in the Kyoto style, and Japanese sauces/seasonings are used throughout. As with most Japanese restaurants, soy sauce and similar seasonings here very likely contain wheat; assume wheat unless staff confirm otherwise.

This is a meat-and-seafood yoshoku house centered on beef stew, fried shrimp, croquettes and cutlets; there are no documented vegan or vegetarian dishes, and shared fryer/grill surfaces make animal-product cross-contact likely. Vegan diners should confirm directly before visiting.

No allergy-handling procedures, allergen menus, or accommodation policies are documented in any available source. With reservation-only seating and a tiny owner-run kitchen, the best path is to phone ahead and discuss needs directly.

The restaurant is small, owner-run and reservation-based, so staff can be spoken with directly about ingredients before or at booking, the kind of personal kitchen where a careful conversation is possible.

name: お昼ごはんとおやつ カフェ日々 (Cafe Hibi (Ohiru-gohan to Oyatsu Cafe Hibi))

claims.text: No information on cross-contamination controls is available from any source. Bread baking (wheat flour) is the kitchen's core daily activity, making airborne flour a realistic concern for highly sensitive individuals.
Standard Japanese soy sauce (containing wheat) is likely used in savoury dishes such as curry; no tamari or gluten-free soy sauce alternative is documented.
Dairy and eggs are used throughout the menu (custard pudding, bread, cakes); shared prep surfaces are probable in this very small kitchen.
No allergy-handling procedures are mentioned in any reviewed source. The cafe can be contacted by phone on 026-232-0239 to ask directly.
Uses domestic wheat and Hoshino natural yeast; offers organic leaf teas and caffeine-free rooibos — some ingredient mindfulness is present even if allergen labelling is absent.

No information is published about the soba kitchen's wheat-handling practices. Traditional soba shops often mix in wheat flour (up to 20–30%) to help noodles bind; it is unknown whether this shop does so or processes wheat products on the same surfaces as its soba.
The tsuyu (dipping sauce) is a standard Japanese bonito-based soy sauce broth. Standard Japanese shoyu contains wheat; no wheat-free soy sauce alternative is mentioned at this restaurant.

Bonito (katsuo) is the base of all broth at this restaurant; there is no plant-based broth option. Tempura is fried in shared oil. Complete avoidance of fish-derived ingredients is not possible from the standard menu.
No allergen menu, allergy inquiry process, or staff allergy-handling protocol has been documented at this restaurant across any reviewed source.
Noodles are made fresh on-site daily (打ち立て・茹でたて), so the buckwheat itself is freshly milled — a positive for quality, though it does not imply any allergen controls.

name: そば処とがくし (Soba Dokoro Togakushi)

claims.text: Udon (100% wheat) is prepared and served in the same 11-seat counter kitchen alongside soba. Cross-contamination with wheat flour is highly probable. No separation noted in any source.
Dipping tsuyu is described as sharp and soy-forward, consistent with standard wheat-containing soy sauce. No tamari or GF soy sauce alternative is mentioned in any source.
All broth is katsuobushi (bonito) based. No kombu-only or vegan dashi option is noted. Animal-stock contact is unavoidable.
Solo elderly owner; no allergy handling, allergen menu, or dietary accommodation noted in any source. No English communication indicated. Contact at 026-234-2670 if needed.
Buckwheat soba itself is a naturally gluten-free grain; the noodles are hand-cut by the owner from Togakushi-sourced flour — no industrial additives noted.
